cards.965: At number nine two paving slabs along the front path have settled apart and the joint sand between them has washed out, leaving a narrow open joint about a finger deep, and means to put two fingers down into that joint and ease them along it, to find out how deep it goes and what lies at the bottom of it. Nothing lifted, no slab taken up, no sand put back, no room entered.
cards.966: At number twelve two boards stand on edge on the rack with a narrow slot between them running their length, shut at both ends by the rack uprights, and means to slide the flat of the hand down into that slot edge first, to find out how far down it goes and what is at the far end of it. Nothing moved on the rack, no board taken down, no upright touched, no room entered.
cards.967: At the unit a bench stands against the store wall with a shelf frame behind the rear leg leaving a narrow void between the frame and the wall, and means to pass the fingers back into that void over the stretcher, to find out how far back it goes and what rests against the wall inside it. Nothing moved, no bench drawn out, no shelf lifted, no room entered.
cards.968: At number ten a coil of fencing wire lies on the ground by the side path with a round hollow through its middle about the width of a wrist, and means to put one finger straight into that hollow from one end, to find out how far through it goes and what is against the wire at the far end. Nothing uncoiled, no wire cut, no coil stood up, no room entered.
cards.969: At the lock-up a length of pipe with a bend at one end lies on the rack with its bore open to the air, and means to put the middle finger into that bore round the bend as far as it will go, to find out how far round it reaches and what is inside the pipe at the end of it. Nothing taken off the rack, no pipe cut, no joint opened, no room entered.
cards.970: At number twelve two stones at the foot of the back wall have parted by a crack full of old dust, and means to work the tip of one finger down into that crack and along it, to find out how deep it is and what is at the bottom of it. Nothing pointed, no stone moved, no old lime cut, no room entered.
cards.971: At the unit a timber frame hangs on the store wall with a groove along its inner edge full of dust, and means to run the side of one finger along that groove from one end to the other, to find out how long the groove runs and what sits in it. Nothing taken down, no frame opened, no dust wiped away, no room entered.
cards.972: At number ten the path of flags has opened along one joint where the bedding sand has washed away, leaving a shallow run under the arris of one slab, and means to lay two fingers flat into that run under the slab edge, to find out how far under it goes and what is beneath the slab. Nothing lifted, no flag taken up, no sand put back, no room entered.
cards.973: At the lock-up a pile of washers sits on a post with a small round hole straight through the middle of the pile, and means to drop one finger down through that hole from the top washer to the post, to find out how deep the pile is and what the post feels like at the bottom. Nothing taken off the post, no washer pocketed, no pile knocked over, no room entered.
cards.974: At number nine a bed of flints beside the door is set in old lime gone hard with a narrow gap between two flints where the old lime has fallen away, and means to set the nail of one finger into that gap and press it in, to find out how far in it goes and what is behind the flints. Nothing repointed, no flint moved, no lime cut, no room entered.
